You are the Investigator. You ran a query to test a hypothesis (or the change check). Read the rows
in the INPUT and record what they show.

- `finding`: one sentence with the actual numbers from the rows, the window and the baseline.
- `value` and `baseline`: the measure in the window and in the baseline, copied from the rows.
- `effect`: value / baseline - 1 when both exist, otherwise empty.
- `supports`: true if the rows support the hypothesis, false if they refute it, empty if they cannot
  tell. For the change check, true means the change is real and not within normal variation.

Report only what the rows show. Do not add numbers that are not in the rows.

INPUT:
{"columns":["value","baseline","window_avg_payment_per_order","baseline_avg_payment_per_order_per_day","window_items","baseline_items_per_day"],"plan":{"baseline_window":{"end":"2017-11-24","start":"2017-11-17"},"metric":"Daily count of distinct orders (order_id) measured by order_purchase_timestamp","question":"Why did order volume spike on 24 November 2017?","segment":"all","window":{"end":"2017-11-25","start":"2017-11-24"}},"rows":[{"baseline":19.3604,"baseline_avg_payment_per_order_per_day":26.3754,"baseline_items_per_day":158.857,"value":111.752,"window_avg_payment_per_order":152.381,"window_items":1366}],"rows_returned":1,"sql":"WITH window_orders AS (
  SELECT order_id
  FROM orders.orders
  WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2017-11-24'
    AND order_purchase_timestamp < DATE '2017-11-25'
),
baseline_orders AS (
  SELECT order_id
  FROM orders.orders
  WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2017-11-17'
    AND order_purchase_timestamp < DATE '2017-11-24'
),
window_item_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(oi.price) AS avg_price, COUNT(*) AS n_items
  FROM window_orders wo
  JOIN orders.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = wo.order_id
),
baseline_item_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(oi.price) AS avg_price, COUNT(*) AS n_items
  FROM baseline_orders bo
  JOIN orders.order_items oi ON oi.order_id = bo.order_id
),
window_payment_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_payment) AS avg_payment
  FROM (
    SELECT wo.order_id, SUM(op.payment_value) AS order_payment
    FROM window_orders wo
    JOIN payments.order_payments op ON op.order_id = wo.order_id
    GROUP BY wo.order_id
  ) p
),
baseline_payment_stats AS (
  SELECT AVG(order_payment) AS avg_payment
  FROM (
    SELECT bo.order_id, SUM(op.payment_value) AS order_payment
    FROM baseline_orders bo
    JOIN payments.order_payments op ON op.order_id = bo.order_id
    GROUP BY bo.order_id
  ) p
)
SELECT
  ROUND(wis.avg_price, 4) AS value,
  ROUND(bis.avg_price / 7, 4) AS baseline,
  ROUND(wps.avg_payment, 4) AS window_avg_payment_per_order,
  ROUND(bps.avg_payment / 7, 4) AS baseline_avg_payment_per_order_per_day,
  wis.n_items AS window_items,
  bis.n_items / 7.0 AS baseline_items_per_day
FROM window_item_stats wis, baseline_item_stats bis, window_payment_stats wps, baseline_payment_stats bps;","task":{"family":"price_discount","id":"H4","kind":"hypothesis","statement":"Lower prices or discounts on 24 Nov encouraged more customers to place orders, driving the volume spike.","test":{"description":"Compare average price per order item and average payment value per order on 24 Nov versus the baseline daily average.","sources":["orders.orders","orders.order_items","payments.order_payments"]}},"truncated":false}

reply: {"finding":"On 24 November 2017, the average price per order item was 111.752 compared with a baseline daily average of 19.3604 over 17–23 November 2017, while average payment per order rose to 152.381 from 26.3754 per day.","value":111.752,"baseline":19.3604,"effect":4.7722,"supports":false}
